etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English destourben, from Anglo-Norman distourber and Old French destorber, from Latin disturbare, intensifying for turbare (“to throw into disorder”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)twerH-, *(s)turH- (“to rotate, swirl, twirl, move around”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) to confuse a quiet, constant state or a calm, continuous flow, in particular: thoughts, actions or liquids.
(transitive) to divert, redirect, or alter by disturbing.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) to have a negative emotional impact; to cause emotional distress or confusion.
